items.article_context_en: SATS will offer a fixed 15% dividend yield at par and be junior to the company's existing SATA, which pays a variable rate (currently 13%). Bitcoin treasury company Strive ASST$27.60·Market Closed on Tuesday evening announced a new perpetual preferred stock, SATS, with a 15% fixed dividend. The company is aiming to sell 5 million shares at $100 per share, for a capital raise of $500 million, with proceeds to be used to purchase additional bitcoin BTC$83,498.63, acquire income-producing assets, or buy back stock. The new share class will sit junior to Strive’s current perpetual preferred, SATA, which has a variable rate (currently 13%). At closing of the offering, the company intends to establish a dividend reserve equal to the first 18 months of dividend payments on SATS. Unlike most bitcoin treasury companies, including far larger peer Strategy, Strive has in recent weeks been able to significantly increase its bitcoin holdings. The company last week acquired 3,311 bitcoin, bringing total holdings to 32,773 coins, currently worth about $2.7 billiion. Three months ago, holdings were below 20,000 coins. items.article_summary_en: A new cryptocurrency exchange will allow investors to speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence (AI) giants like OpenAI and Anthropic when they go public. MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. The platform, built on MegaETH blockchain, raised $6.4 million from investors led by Village Global in June. Unlike Bitget’s perpetual futures which never expire, MNX offers contracts with expiration dates at the end of 2027 and incur no recurring funding fees.
items.article_context_en: MNX is offering a different way to trade the future valuations of private AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek. A new cryptocurrency exchange will allow investors to speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence (AI) giants like OpenAI and Anthropic when they go public. MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. The platform, built on MegaETH blockchain, raised $6.4 million from investors led by Village Global in June. Larger crypto exchanges, including OKX and Bitget, already offer contracts that let traders bet on the value of private AI companies without owning their shares. Unlike Bitget’s perpetual futures which never expire, MNX offers contracts with expiration dates at the end of 2027 and incur no recurring funding fees. OKX also offers contracts with no expiration dates, but uses a different funding mechanism. The investment is a bet that financial markets have yet to catch up with the enormous amounts of money flowing into artificial intelligence, according to Village Global. "AI is driving one of the largest investment cycles in history, despite the financial infrastructure around it remaining quite underdeveloped," said Max Killberg of Village Global. He said the firm sees an opportunity to develop financial markets around AI, rather than simply back another prediction market. Manifold Markets co-founder Stephen Gruggett told CoinDesk that MNX’s approach is better suited to private companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, whose shares trade infrequently and are difficult to price. "OpenAI, Anthropic secondaries are illiquid and hard to price," he said. "A perp based on an illiquid, stale price is worse than meaningless: it doesn't behave the way investors expect; it's easy to manipulate; and it may have a very high and unpredictable funding rate." Traders can also use up to three times their available funds, increasing both potential profits and losses. Prices are determined by trading activity on MNX rather than an external price feed.

The unidentified trader, pseudonymously “realist” on X, said attackers held him at knifepoint, destroyed his phone and forced transfers of approximately $40,000 from a hot wallet and $720,000 from his Ledger wallet. The trader shared a Solana wallet address on blockchain explorer Solscan to substantiate his account, though there has yet been no corresponding confirmation from the police or other authorities regarding the incident. and do crypto get the f**k out,” he posted. The incident follows recent reports of a similar U.K. robbery last December, where masked attackers beat a cryptocurrency investor with hammers and threatened to kill his pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds in crypto. Such crimes, commonly called “wrench attacks,” involve physical violence or threats to compel crypto holders to surrender their assets. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimates criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026. Home invasions accounted for 37% of recorded incidents, up from 14% a year earlier. France emerged as a hotspot for wrench attacks, with Chainalysis documenting at least 30 recorded incidents in the first half of this year. Blockchain security firm Certik identified 52 verified attacks globally during that period, of which 33 were in France. The figures suggest physical coercion is becoming an increasingly significant concern alongside wholly digital threats such as hacks, phishing and smart-contract exploits. The implications for investors extend beyond protecting private keys to keeping holdings confidential, limiting public disclosures about one’s trading activity and separating readily available funds from long-term reserves.

items.article_summary_en: South Korea’s FIU approved measures blocking domestic web access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted. The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. South Korean investors have been gradually moving large amounts of crypto overseas for months due to stricter rules, with an estimated $110 billion leaving domestic exchanges in 2025.
items.article_context_en: South Korea’s FIU approved measures blocking domestic web access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges. The country’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) announced Tuesday that the Korea Communications Standards Commission approved the restrictions following reviews on Oct. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted. The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. Regulators can now seek website blocks as soon as they detect unregistered activity, without waiting for a court ruling or evidence that customers have lost money. The FIU did not specify how long the restrictions will last or set a deadline for the exchanges to register. However, any exchange that wants to legally operate in the country and serve South Korean customers must register with the FIU and meet the country’s security and anti-money laundering (AML) requirements. “We respect applicable laws and regulations across jurisdictions and continuously strengthen our compliance framework in response to evolving regulatory requirements,” a KuCoin spokesperson said. “User assets remain safe and secure, and we will communicate any further updates through our official channels.” BitMart, Phemex and MEXC did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment. South Korea's proposed Digital Asset Basic Law, yet to come into force, would set the groundwork for a legal framework for digital assets, including issuance, trading, custody and supervision. The country’s Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory service announced new rules in April, removing the discretion exchanges had to let users bypass holding periods. The FIU said it has referred 44 unregistered operators to investigators and will seek further blocks against websites that reopen under different addresses. Only 28 virtual asset service providers are currently registered with the regulator. The financial watchdog also warned that traders using unauthorized platforms could face difficulties recovering their funds.

items.article_context_en: 13, 2026 While major cryptocurrencies remain choppy, STX, the native token of the Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, is rallying. The cryptocurrency has surged nearly 10% in 24 hours, 14% over the past week and more than 50% in four weeks, outperforming bitcoin BTC$83,498.63, ether ETH$2,497.90, XRP (XRP) and other cryptocurrencies. The outperformance likely reflects investor interest in Stacks’ non-custodial bitcoin staking architecture. This framework lets BTC holders stake and earn yield directly on the main Bitcoin blockchain while retaining strict control of their private keys. In contrast, traditional frameworks require users to wrap their assets into synthetic tokens (like wBTC) or move funds over cross-chain bridges to earn additional yield. Stacks’ framework relies on a mechanism called "bonding," which requires participants to lock up assets to secure the network. The "Bonding Period 3,” due in November, requires participants holding native STX to lock a specific ratio of STX alongside their BTC — equivalent to roughly 5% of the total value of their BTC — to successfully secure protocol stacking capacity. This creates a positive feedback loop for STX: As more BTC moves into the Stacks ecosystem, a larger portion of STX is systematically locked up and removed from the active market. By tying bitcoin liquidity directly to STX scarcity, the architecture skews demand-supply dynamics heavily in favor of long-term price appreciation. Period 3 follows Periods 1 and 2, which served as preparatory phases to safely transition signers and bootstrap initial liquidity. STX is not the only coin to have surged over 24 hours. BDX, REDNER, and PYTH are other major gainers, adding 6% each. It’s a sign of liquidity increasingly pivoting to coins other than the major cryptocurrencies. Still, the broader context remains tightly bound to macroeconomic indicators.

items.article_context_en: Sberbank plans to open crypto trading to all clients Dec. 1 and is already testing BTC, ETH and USDT trades in its app. The Bank of Russia added Sberbank to its register of cryptocurrency exchange providers, according to Interfax. The bank had already joined the digital depository register earlier this month, giving it a role in recording clients’ crypto holdings. There are now nine organizations on the exchange register, including VTB and T-Invest Lab. The approval marks another step away from the central bank’s 2022 proposal to ban domestic crypto exchanges and prohibit Russian financial intermediaries from handling cryptocurrencies. 1 instead creates a regulated market involving banks, brokers, exchanges and digital depositories. The two registrations cover different parts of that market. Registered crypto dealers can buy and sell cryptocurrencies using their own funds outside organized exchanges, while depositories record ownership and transfers, according to the central bank. The combination provides a route to offer both trading and custody-related services for Sberbank, having also started working on a crypto wallet earlier this year. That opening comes with tighter control over how investors hold and move their coins. Domestic crypto payments remain prohibited, and the central bank says that from July of next year, crypto transactions will have to go through registered intermediaries. That would effectively shut out peer-to-peer transactions settled through Russian bank accounts. Sberbank plans to debut its first products Dec.

items.article_summary_en: South Korea’s stock market suffered another sharp selloff on Tuesday, with the KOSPI falling 5.5% during Asian trading. The index is now roughly 38% below its June all-time high, extending a reversal that contrasts with bitcoin’s 40% recovery. Bitcoin bottomed near $58,000 shortly after the KOSPI peaked and has since rebounded as high as $87,000. The weekly chart shows a 20 day-period rolling correlation of -0.41, indicating a moderately negative relationship between bitcoin and the KOSPI.
items.article_context_en: South Korea’s chipmakers lead another sharp selloff as concerns over AI spending and Chinese competition grow, while bitcoin holds well above its summer lows. South Korea’s stock market suffered another sharp selloff on Tuesday, with the KOSPI falling 5.5% during Asian trading. The index is now roughly 38% below its June all-time high, extending a reversal that contrasts with bitcoin’s 40% recovery. Bitcoin bottomed near $58,000 shortly after the KOSPI peaked and has since rebounded as high as $87,000. The weekly chart shows a 20 day-period rolling correlation of -0.41, indicating a moderately negative relationship between bitcoin and the KOSPI. That divergence suggests that bitcoin could benefit as investors reduce exposure to the AI trade, although correlation alone does not establish capital rotation. The latest selloff followed comments from Broadcom (AVGO) CEO Hock Tan likening speculative AI investing to gambling in a casino, according to the Financial Times. His remarks intensified concerns about whether the industry can generate returns sufficient to justify enormous infrastructure spending. In addition, advances by Chinese memory-chip rival CXMT added to fears about competition and the durability of chipmakers’ margins, according to Bloomberg. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics fell around 10% and 7%, respectively. premarket trading, with memory and storage chipmakers Micron Technology (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) both down around 3%. items.article_summary_en: Onchain researchers estimate the Ledger supply-chain breach drained up to $93.2 million across 300 wallets. Covert hardware implanted in some Ledger crypto wallet devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis read users’ 24-word recovery phrases from the gadget screen and sent them to an attacker over a mobile phone network, Ledger said Tuesday in an investigation update on X. Ledger also released a statement on X saying MediaMarkt Saturn stopped selling its devices, following a report of a “spy” implant from one customer in Germany. Onchain researchers, however, estimated the losses were up to $93.2 million across more than 300 wallets, with Tether freezing $10 million of its dollar-pegged stablecoin USDT tied to the theft.
items.article_context_en: Onchain researchers estimate the Ledger supply-chain breach drained up to $93.2 million across 300 wallets. Covert hardware implanted in some Ledger crypto wallet devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis read users’ 24-word recovery phrases from the gadget screen and sent them to an attacker over a mobile phone network, Ledger said Tuesday in an investigation update on X. Ledger said the spy chip sat inside the device enclosure. When a user set up the signer and the screen displayed the recovery phrase, the implant’s microcontroller recognized and decoded the words, then transmitted them over LTE, a data transmission technology used by cellphones, utilizing an eSIM. The recovery phrase is the master key to a crypto wallet. Anyone who has it can recreate the wallet elsewhere and move the funds without needing the physical Ledger device or changing any transactions on it. The account is the first public explanation of the mechanism behind the CryptoBilis-linked thefts. Ledger said the implant did not modify the device’s secure Element, the chip designed to protect private keys, or its operating system. It also did not alter transactions or signatures. The incident was a physical supply chain attack rather than a breach of Ledger’s software or internal systems. Ledger also took to X to announce that the investigations will continue until they determine who tampered with their devices and new policies around resellers. “Ledger is reviewing its reseller controls and anti-tamper protections,” CTO Charles Guillemet said on X. “We invite researchers and other vendors to work with us on tamper-detection and chain-of-custody practices.” Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier said Ledger is “reviewing the controls that apply to our direct sales and to resellers, and we will share what we can.” He also said the CryptoBilis has topped selling Ledger signers and that the “investigation is ongoing to determine who tampered with these signers or where in the distribution chain it happened.” Mark Karpeles, the former CEO of bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox, claimed he found a spy implant in a Ledger Flex bought at the Singapore Airport.
